title: The absolute truth
prompt:
The value register starts at `-42`, and the program should print its magnitude: `42`.

Compare the register against zero, skip the sign flip when it is already positive, and flip it otherwise. `neg` produces the negation of a register in one instruction.

Once it passes, change the starting value to `42` and run again: the same code has to leave a positive value alone.

## what is checked

- the magnitude is printed on its own line
- the program exits cleanly
- the sign flip uses `neg`
starter:
// print the absolute value of a signed register
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(value_r, x19)

        .data
fmt:    .string "magnitude = %lld\n"

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     value_r, -42

        // TODO: if value_r is negative, flip its sign so the
        // printf below prints the magnitude

        ldr     x0, =fmt
        mov     x1, value_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
